9250-a-book-of-autographs.title: A Book Of Autographs
9250-a-book-of-autographs.creator: Unknown
9250-a-book-of-autographs.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. There are several letters from John Adams, written in a small, hasty, ungraceful hand, but earnest, and with no unnecessary flourish. The earliest is dated at Philadelphia, September 26, 1774, about twenty days after the first opening of the Continental Congress. We look at this old yellow document, scribbled on half a sheet of foolscap, and ask of it many questions for which words have no response.

arxiv-2307-10972.title: Adaptively Weighted Audits of Instant-Runoff Voting Elections: AWAIRE Thanks: Authors listed alphabetically. Published in: Electronic Voting, E-Vote-ID 2023, LNCS 14230, pp. 35–51, Springer, Cham (2023). https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-43756-4˙3
arxiv-2307-10972.creator: Alexander Ek, Philip B. Stark, Peter J. Stuckey, Damjan Vukcevic
arxiv-2307-10972.description: Abstract An election audit is risk-limiting if the audit limits (to a pre-specified threshold) the chance that an erroneous electoral outcome will be certified. Extant methods for auditing instant-runoff voting (IRV) elections are either not risk-limiting or require cast vote records (CVRs), the voting system’s electronic record of the votes on each ballot.

arxiv-2403-04808.title: WaterMax: breaking the LLM watermark detectability-robustness-quality trade-off
arxiv-2403-04808.creator: Eva Giboulot, Teddy Furon
arxiv-2403-04808.description: Abstract Watermarking is a technical means to dissuade malfeasant usage of Large Language Models. This paper proposes a novel watermarking scheme, so-called WaterMax, that enjoys high detectability while sustaining the quality of the generated text of the original LLM. Its new design leaves the LLM untouched (no modification of the weights, logits, temperature, or sampling technique).

arxiv-2405-15444.title: HINT: Hypernetwork Approach to Training Weight Interval Regions in Continual Learning
arxiv-2405-15444.creator: Patryk Krukowski, Anna Bielawska, Kamil Książek Paweł Wawrzyński Paweł Batorski Przemysław Spurek
arxiv-2405-15444.description: Abstract Recently, a new Continual Learning (CL) paradigm was presented to control catastrophic forgetting, called Interval Continual Learning (InterContiNet), which relies on enforcing interval constraints on the neural network parameter space. Unfortunately, InterContiNet training is challenging due to the high dimensionality of the weight space, making intervals difficult to manage.

arxiv-2503-01587.title: The State-Dependent Riccati Equation in Nonlinear Optimal Control: Analysis and Numerical Approximation
arxiv-2503-01587.creator: Luca Saluzzi
arxiv-2503-01587.description: Abstract The State-Dependent Riccati Equation (SDRE) approach is extensively utilized in nonlinear optimal control as a reliable framework for designing robust feedback control strategies. This work provides an analysis of the SDRE approach, examining its theoretical foundations, error bounds, and numerical approximation techniques.

arxiv-2503-04694.description: Abstract Rapid resource model updating with real-time data is important for making timely decisions in resource management and mining operations. This requires optimal merging of models and observations, which can be achieved through data assimilation, and the ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) has become a popular method for this task.

pmc-7619520.title: Kandinsky: Enabling neighbourhood analysis of spatial omics data for functional insights on cell ecosystems
pmc-7619520.creator: Pietro Andrei, Mariachiara Grieco, Amelia Acha-Sagredo, Tommaso Becchi, Pawan Dhami, Kathy Fung, Manuel Rodriguez-Justo, Matteo Cereda, Francesca D Ciccarelli
pmc-7619520.description: AimsSpatially resolved omics technologies enable investigation of cellular interactions within their local microenvironments (neighbourhoods) directly in situ. Although several computational methods have been developed for neighbourhood analysis, significant limitations remain in how neighbourhoods are defined and interrogated. Here, we present Kandinsky, a toolkit that provides a flexible and versatile framework for defining and analysing cell neighbourhoods.
